title: Tinnitus Activities Treatment Update: Managing Attention and Auditory Attention
content: Attentional complaints are among the most prevalent debilitating features reported by individuals with chronic tinnitus. Concentration problems related to tinnitus are frequently underestimated by clinicians. Tinnitus Activities Treatment (TAT) is an established, person-centered management approach addressing thoughts and emotions, hearing, sleep, and concentration. A synthesis was conducted of recent empirical findings, educational paradigms, and updated person-centered practices that incorporate the Tinnitus Activities Treatment approach. Personalized approaches to the management of attention and auditory attention were examined. The framework of Tinnitus Activities Treatment incorporates targeted practical activities designed to shift the focus of attention away from the tinnitus. The process follows a logical, step-by-step sequence. It should be structured around directing attention, alternating the focus of attention, and subsequently shifting that focus away from tinnitus. Tinnitus Activities Treatment’s approach has a dual emphasis on strengthening executive cognitive control to mitigate general distraction and, simultaneously, reeducating selective auditory attention.
